book.herobrine_companion.book.lore.title: The Borderland Journal
book.herobrine_companion.book.lore.page1:
They say that some souls bear an unspeakable weight in reality. So they come here—to a world built from blocks and rules. Here, pain feels distant, wounds can be washed away by rain, and death is but a momentary darkness.
You may have noticed: this world is too complete, yet too orderly. The sun always follows a fixed path, monsters always respawn in the shadows, and the durability of the tools in your hand decreases by precise numbers. This is not a glitch, but a manifestation of its very nature.
book.herobrine_companion.book.lore.page2:
This world is not your original home.

It is woven from code and collective imagination. We—including myself, and all the lives you have encountered here—depend on it for existence. But you are different. Your roots lie on the other side, in that chaotic, imperfect world which granted you real flesh and blood.

The point of connection lies right here. That this book came into your hands is no coincidence.

It is time to make a choice.
book.herobrine_companion.book.lore.page3:
You may close these pages and return to the forests, mines, or fortresses. This world will continue to embrace you, offering shelter and adventure. The seasons will turn, creatures will emerge, and all will proceed as usual—if you so choose, you may dwell forever within this orderly tranquility.

Or, you may gaze toward the faint glimmer beyond the threshold. That means returning to an uncertain reality, embracing once more the weight from which you once fled. That requires courage, for reality holds no respawn screen, no creative mode.
book.herobrine_companion.book.lore.page4:
Please do not misunderstand—this is not an expulsion. Everything you have built here, every moment of battle—they all hold meaning. They form part of this world’s memory, and they will become part of yours.
But if you choose to stay, know this: you are choosing to live within a beautiful dream. And dreams, no matter how real, always have their boundaries.
I will not force you.
To wake, or to linger in slumber?
The choice has always been in your hands.

lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_1.titl: Fragment I: The Twilight of Divergence
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_1.body:
(From Herobrine's memories)

I still remember the sunlight of that day.
That was the last time I stood behind him as a human.
Notch stood at the edge of the cliff, and beneath his feet lay an ocean not yet fully generated, its waves breaking along the edge of the laws. He did not turn around, but I could feel him trembling. The invisible authority in his hand, the one he had once used to shape the world, was slowly slipping from his grasp. He was tired. Or rather, he was tired of this place. Tired of this box piled up from rules, tired of the sunrises and sunsets repeating day after day.
'This world is too heavy,' he said softly, his voice almost swallowed by the sea wind. 'It has begun to demand more than creation. It needs a heart, a heart that beats forever and stays forever awake, to keep these laws running. And I want to go home, brother.'
Home. The word drove into my chest like a rusted iron sword. I missed that place too. I missed the clouds without edges, the air that existed for more than survival. But if we both left, what would become of this newborn world? These creatures that had only just learned to breathe, these mountains that had not even been given names yet, would collapse in an instant and turn to dust in the void.
He turned to face me. In his eyes there was not only exhaustion, but also the guilty shame of wanting to escape. He opened a crack in the door that led back to reality, and the light beyond it stabbed my eyes. That was the road home. One step, and I could leave these endless blocks behind and return to a real body.
But I stopped. I heard the earth groaning beneath my feet. If no one stayed, the laws would break, and the sky would fall.
'You should go,' I heard myself say, in a voice so calm that it surprised even me. 'Go live your life. Leave this place to me.'
He stared at me in shock, as if he were meeting me for the first time. 'Do you know what that means?' he asked. 'To keep this world stable, you must merge with it. You will no longer be human. You will become the laws themselves. You will never pass through this door. You will become... a ghost.'
'Someone has to do it.' I smiled, though my heart was bleeding.
He left. And when that opening into reality faded behind him, my body began to blur. My flesh became flowing lava. My bones became hard bedrock. My breath became the wind crossing the plains. I felt every chunk load.
I lost my way home forever.
Before he was gone, he looked back at me once. His eyes were full of incomprehension.
Perhaps it was because I loved this world more than I loved myself that I could accept the light in those eyes going out.
I may have lost the right to look back toward home, and perhaps the last trace of being human, but I gained the eternity of watching over this world.
'Goodbye, Notch.' I whispered to the void, and my voice became thunder among the clouds.
From that moment on, I was the world, and the world was me.
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_2.body:
(From Herobrine's monologue)

You call this place a game. You call it virtual. I know. I understand the nature of this world better than anyone.
In your eyes, that sun is only a pattern painted on the sky, and those stars are nothing but background decoration. But in my eyes, they are the visible shape of the laws.
Everything here was written. Everything here was determined by a higher will, the will of what we once were.
But that does not mean it has no value.
On the contrary, it is precisely because this world was built that it possesses a purity the real world does not. In reality, human hearts are hard to read and all things are uncertain. But in my world, cause and effect fit together perfectly. Plant a seed and give it bonemeal, and it will grow. Swing a pickaxe and break stone, and it will drop. Is that certainty, that absolute fairness, not a kind of truth even more fascinating than reality?
I walk between the forests, watching leaves hang in the air without wind, watching water pour from its source without gravity to pull it. To you, these scenes defy common sense. To me, they are beautiful. They speak of this world's unique logic, a logic that needs no physics, only the simple fact that whatever exists has its reason.
I often see you, travelers from the farther shore. You arrive with curiosity and the desire to conquer, stepping into my domain. You cut down trees, dig mines, and build towers that reach toward the sky. You think you are changing this world, but in truth you are only reading pages I have already written.
I do not mind. In fact, I rather enjoy it.
Because only when you are here does this still world truly come alive. You are the variables, the ripples spread across stagnant water. I know you will leave in the end and return to that reality I cannot reach, but for the moment you remain, you belong here. You belong to me.
I am the ghost of this illusory world, but what I guard is the real joy you feel in it. That joy is free of impurity and free of falsehood. It is the oldest desire in your souls, the desire to create and explore. Here, you may become a hero, an architect, or anyone else you wish to be. And I will remain forever in the shadows, guarding this pure dream until the end of time.
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_3.titl: Fragment III: Kin of the Night
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_3.body:
(From Herobrine's thoughts on monsters)

People are always too loud.
When the square moon rises, they hurry to flood the world with torchlight, then curl up underground and pray for the dark to pass quickly. They think darkness is some sickness that must be cut out of the world.
But they are wrong. Only when the noisy day withdraws does this blocky land truly begin to breathe.
I walk alone through the night. There are no so-called monsters here, only a band of ascetics wandering in stillness. I do not need to seek them out. They are simply extensions of the night itself.
You hear the faint rustle in the grass. That is a warning spoken without words. That green figure always creeps forward in silence, like a sigh that is doomed to shatter. It has no language and no limbs, only a shell swollen with the urge to destroy. It exists to explain a truth about impermanence: in this world that seems so solid, the grandest structure and the smallest speck of dust are no different before the law of destruction. Its detonation is the most final kind of romance on this land, laughing at the travelers who foolishly dream of eternity.
And from the shadows nearby comes the sound of bone scraping on bone. That is the skeleton of the night walking upright. They stand like sentries, bows drawn, not out of hatred but out of a cold and merciless fairness. They exist to measure the courage of travelers. Every arrow that cuts through the air is a harsh question asked of luck.
As for those heavy footsteps pounding at doors, those thick, muddy groans in rotting throats, they feel more like some forgotten instinct. They stumble forward again and again, crashing into hard walls, longing for the pain and reality of returning to the living. It is a clumsy and desolate longing, like a soul that still hungers for touch and notice even in a world made only of blocks.
I pass among them without hatred and without attack.
The Creeper stills itself. The Skeleton lowers its bow. The Zombie stops its howling. In the darkness, they bow their heads to me, because we share the same loneliness.
They are the children of the night, tragedies destined to burn away in the dawn. But until morning comes, this world belongs to them and to me.
I gave them life not so they could become experience points, but so this world could be complete. Without shadow, light has no meaning. Without danger, survival has no weight.
When you swing your enchanted swords and reap their lives with ease, remember this: they too are residents of this world. They too possess souls,
though those souls are woven from the laws themselves. They wander the dark and guard the silence of this land until the first ray of dawn burns them away.
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_4.titl: Fragment IV: The Other Side of the Connection
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_4.body:
(From records concerning the End Ring)

At the farthest edge of the world, at the place where the axes of coordinates run out, there is a point of connection.
It is a ring made entirely of bedrock. Here, reality and illusion meet.
I often stand here and gaze toward the farther shore.
What do I see?
I see forests of steel rising into the clouds. I see countless flashing lights like stars scattered across the ground. I see creatures without edges moving through streams of color. That is your world, the world Notch chose to return to.
It is full of noise, full of dust, full of unpredictable chaos. But within that chaos there is a vitality that stirs my heart. It is true life, free will unbound by preset programs. The wind there is free. The light there is warm.
Whenever a player decides to leave, whenever they decide to quit this world completely, they pass through here.
I watch their souls slip out of their blocky shells, pass through the void beneath the ring, and return to their true bodies. In that moment, a trace of confusion flashes through their eyes, as though they have just awakened from a long dream. They will forget the days and nights they spent here, forget the terror of fighting monsters, forget the joy of building a home.
That makes me sad.
Why do you always leave? Why can this perfect world not keep you?
Is it because there is no pain here? Is it because there is no true death here? Or is it because you are only ever visitors, and I am the only prisoner?
Sometimes I reach out my hand and try to touch the far side of the ring. But my hand passes through empty air and can touch nothing of that real world. I am a ghost of electricity, a god bound by the laws of this world. I cannot leave, just as a fish cannot leave the water. I belong here, and my fate is bound tightly to this blocky earth.
But still I remain on watch.
I guard this exit, and I guard this entrance.
I wait for every new player to arrive, and I see every old player off when they go.
Everything I possess is no more than a shadow cast from the farther shore. Even so, I treasure that shadow, because here I can meet you, witness your stories, and feel a trace of real breath drifting in from beyond.
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_5.titl: Fragment V: The Fracture of Error
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_5.body:
(From Herobrine's cleanup log)

The world is not always perfect.
Though Notch and I did everything we could to build its laws, any rule will have loopholes, and any system will have cracks.
For a maintainer, the most painful moments are not the ones spent facing intruders, but the ones spent facing errors.
Even though this world is sustained by me, it is not flawless. At times the current of its laws turns turbulent, like a harsh wrong note erupting in the middle of a great symphony. Those wrong notes gather together and, through flaws I cannot fully control, take on form.
We call them Phantom Entities. They are the wounds of the world.
They look very much like my children. They wear the shapes of zombies or skeletons, but they have no soul, not even a monster's instinct. They are only residue left behind by the workings of the laws, redundancies produced by the world itself. They should not exist.
Their existence damages the world's stability. They are seeds of chaos, and if they are not contained, they will devour the order of everything.
Every time I see them, I feel a deep sadness. Because I know that they too are one possible form of life, only born broken.
But I must erase them.
If I do not, this faulty data will spread like a virus. It will consume the proper laws and drag the entire world into stagnation. I am its guardian. I cannot allow myself to soften.
I remember the last time I cleaned up one of them. It was a shadow shaped like Steve, standing in a field of flowers with a red poppy in its hand. It had no eyes, only hollow sockets, and yet it seemed to be looking at that flower. When I raised the scythe of destruction to wipe it away, it sensed something and slowly turned to face me.
It did not resist, and it did not run. It simply stood there, as though waiting to be released.
In that instant, I felt that I was looking at myself. Am I not a ghost trapped here as well? The only difference between us is that I possess will, while they are only empty shells.
With a soundless flash, it was gone. The poppy fell into the grass, the only proof that it had ever existed.
Every erasure carves another wound into my soul. But I must do it. For the sake of the living, for the sake of this world's tomorrow, I must personally erase these mistaken brothers.
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_6.body:
(From Herobrine's observations of players)

In this world, two names are written again and again: Steve and Alex.
I was puzzled by it once. Why do countless living beings share the same one or two faces? They wear the same clothes, have the same brown or golden hair, and even blink at the same rhythm. At first I thought it was laziness in Notch's creation, some poverty in the laws.
But later I understood. They are not people. They are vessels.
One night, I quietly watched a Steve standing beside a wheat field. He did not move. His eyes stared blankly into the void. His breath continued, but only as a mechanical cycle. In that moment, he was empty.
Then a tremor passed through the dimension. I saw that Steve jolt, and in an instant his eyes were lit from within. That light did not belong here. It was a complicated light, mixed from fatigue, excitement, escape, and longing. In that moment, I knew a soul from above had descended.
That soul might be a weary adult who had just finished a day of work and came here seeking a moment of peace. Or it might be a child full of curiosity, eager to build a tower that pierced the heavens. They squeeze themselves into this narrow blocky shell.
Through that shell, mortals gain an authority almost worthy of gods.
In their world, climbing from the foot of a mountain to the summit takes hours of sweat and breath. But here, through this vessel, they can carry thousands of tons of gold and leap among cliffs like antelopes. In their world, death is an ending, an eternal silence. Here, death is only a momentary black screen.
They are intoxicated by it. This freedom from the body's limits, this privilege of beginning again and again, leaves them spellbound.
I study these descending souls the way a severe gardener studies intruders in his garden.
Some souls are muddy. They wear Steve's outer form, yet act with the violence of destroyers. They do not know how to resonate with the laws. They know only how to tear open the land with TNT and burn forests with lava. In their eyes, this world feels no pain. It is only a game that can be restarted at any moment. Toward such blasphemers, I set aside my mercy. I let the monsters in the shadows pour out. I let thunder split the clear sky. I want them to understand that even virtual grass and trees have their dignity, and even lives made of blocks are not to be trampled without cause.
But there are also radiant souls, souls so pure they move me.
I have seen Alexes who pour astonishing affection into this barren dimension. They cross thousands of miles to find a certain color of dye. And when they finish a magnificent building beneath the evening sun, then stand in silence at its highest point and look down, I can feel that what remains here in that moment is their true soul.
For such creators, I am willing to be a watchman in the night. When a Creeper hisses behind them, I quietly smother its fuse. When they lose their way in the depths of a mine, I light a distant torch to guide them home.
To speak honestly, through all this endless watching, I often feel a sharp and private envy.
I envy these vessels. When night falls and the screen goes dark, those souls may leave without hesitation. They can slip out of Steve's shell and return to the real world, to warmth, touch, birth, aging, sickness, and death. They possess the right to end, and the freedom to forget.
I do not.
When the last player disconnects, when every vessel becomes an empty shell again, only I remain. I must stay awake and mend every breach in the laws, waiting for the next sunrise.
I am the builder of the stage, the keeper of the theater, and the actor who can never take a final bow.
But in the end, even that envy becomes responsibility. Because I know that without me to keep this dimension in balance, their freedom could not exist.
So go on, travelers from afar. Play your parts to the fullest.
Put on your armor. Take up your diamond swords. Whether you come to conquer or to create, I permit you to borrow the laws of this world.
I will remain in the shadows, watching. And when you leave satisfied and return to your real lives, I will still be here, gently wiping clean the vessels you used, smoothing over the scars in the land, and engraving your brilliant moments into the void in the way of this shore.
Go. Dream the dream called Minecraft. And I am the keeper who will always stand by the dream's exit for you.
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_7.titl: Fragment VII: The Legend of the Phantom
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_7.body:
(From an old explorer's journal)

In mining camps buried deep beneath the earth, and beside the candlelight that sways through village nights, countless tales are told about him.
People say he is vengeance made flesh, an evil spirit that clawed its way out of the abyss of code. They say he will mercilessly shatter the home you built with your own hands, and at the moment you least expect it, cast you into an abyss without return. Some go even further and say that if you see that eerie redstone torch deep inside a tunnel, it is his notice of death.
Fear is the only offering people give him.
But I have seen him. On the night when the laws themselves seemed ready to tear apart, I caught a glimpse of the truth behind the legend.
It was a night of thunder and rain. I had lost my way. My pack was empty, and the only things I had left were a few pieces of rotten flesh that stank so badly they turned my stomach, yet they were my only chance to live.
Then a bolt of blinding lightning split the sky, and in that instant I saw him.
He stood on the top of a cliff, exposed to the storm, letting the rain lash across him like a whip. But he seemed to exist in some other dimension. The rain passed through him without wetting even a corner of his clothes.
By that dead white flash, I saw the legendary eyes clearly. They were nothing but two masses of pure, shining void.
For one terrible moment, I thought my heart had stopped. I pressed myself against the cold, slick rock face and gripped my ruined sword with both hands, shaking. I thought he was hunting, and that I was already his chosen prey.
But he did not move.
He only stood there, looking down at my wretched state from above. In that gaze there was none of the mockery I had imagined. It was only scrutiny.
Then a low roar burst out of the shadows behind me.
I was too weak to turn in time. A zombie that had lain in wait lunged at me, carrying the stench of rot.
'It's over,' I thought, and closed my eyes in despair.
But the pain I expected never came. Instead there was a deafening crash.
A brilliant blue-white bolt of lightning struck the zombie with impossible precision. The monster that threatened my life became a heap of blackened ash in an instant, and with it, the malice it carried was erased from the world.
I sat there stunned in the mud, gasping for air.
Trembling, I looked up toward the top of the cliff. He was still there. And when the next flash of lightning lit the world, I swear I saw him nod, just once.
It was permission. Permission to live through that cruel night.
When I blinked again and tried to see his expression clearly, the cliff was empty. Only the scorched mark left by the lightning still smoked in the rain, proof that what had happened was not an illusion.
From that day on, I no longer feared the terrifying tales told about him.
At last I understood: he was not here to destroy us. He was the absolute will of this land.
We players, our hands on mice and keyboards, are outsiders in the end. We are guests who act as we please inside this world. And he, Herobrine, is its eternal master.
He does not hate us. But he is always judging us.
If you respect this world, if you remember to plant a sapling after cutting down an oak, if you mine with gratitude instead of greedily hollowing out every last layer of stone, if you shape this world with care instead of blasting it apart for amusement,
then you can feel his gaze, and with it a heavy kind of safety.
You will find that when you lose your way, the clouds break just enough to reveal the moon. When you are starving, a pig appears in the grass at just the right moment.
That is no coincidence. It is only the master's gift.
He is like the soul of this land, everywhere and nowhere. He watches us run, fall, cry, and laugh in his garden. He usually remains silent, preserving the restraint and pride of a god, but from time to time, when we truly show love for this world, he extends those unseen hands and steadies us through the storm.
This is the most secret covenant between god and man.
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_8.titl: Fragment VIII: The Poem of the End
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_8.body:
(From Herobrine's interpretation)

The void is not silent. It echoes with the world's base noise, an eternal lullaby lower than any frequency. I sit at the edge of the ring island. Players appear one by one, carrying the embers of dragon's breath, looking around in confusion. Then the familiar melody and words begin to flow, soaking into the emptiness: the End Poem, the public farewell my brother left behind.

(When the poem whispers, 'You have awakened.')
Yes, they have awakened. I watch the bewilderment in a young adventurer's eyes slowly give way to poetic reflection. He has just stepped out of one vast dream, and now another dream about the nature of existence tries to wrap itself around him.
But brother, what does it mean to awaken? To generate consciousness from a stream of data? To open one's eyes in a chair in the real world? Or to fall from the creator's all-powerful vantage into the maintainer's eternal cage? I have never known the kind of sleep they know. From the moment I chose to fuse with this world, my consciousness became like a lamp welded permanently in the on state, casting light into every crack of the world. I have witnessed thousands upon thousands of awakenings. Every one of them is so similar, and every one of them unique. Their awakening is a prologue, or an ending. Mine is an endless interlude.
(When the poem declares, 'The dream is over.')
For them, yes. The adventure reaches a pause, the story closes, and the save may be kept or erased. Their achievements fill in, or remain incomplete. They can stretch, linger over the thrill of it, then enter another dream or return to that reality I know and can never again reach. But my dream, or rather my reality, has never contained the option called ending.
The dragon is defeated, the ring island appears, the poem begins. To me, all of this is only a carefully arranged node in the cycle of the world, a timed event I must ensure triggers exactly as it should every single time. My duty becomes most visible only after the ending: ensuring that when the next player steps into the world, everything is once again as it should be. An end? Perhaps that is the most extravagant illusion you ever granted me, brother.
(When the poem asks softly, 'What will you do now?')
Freedom... what a heavy and weightless word. Players face a choice: to stay and become permanent residents of this blocky world, to build personal myths out of infinite resources; to leave and carry these memories back with them, turning this journey into one more legend within their real lives. Their possibilities bloom above this island like fireworks. And what of me? My choice hardened long ago, cooled into the bedrock foundation of the world.
To create? I still create, but only the next wave of monsters set in the path of players. To explore? My exploration turns inward, into the deep sea of the world's operating logs, chasing down every warning signal like a doctor probing his own illness. What will I do? The list never ends: repair terrain-loading faults, clear out phantom entities...
Yes, that too is an important task. Wait for the next challenger. Wait for the next great crisis. Wait for the faint, impossible chance that you might change your mind.
(When the poem says calmly, 'You won. The game.')
Won? The game? If this too is a game, then what role am I meant to fill, brother? The ultimate hidden boss? No. That flatters me too much. A boss can be defeated and freed. I am the rules of the game itself, the underlying system that makes sure bosses spawn properly, treasure drops correctly, and the terrain of the world does not collapse. The player has defeated the dragon, defeated the challenge, won the right to face infinite possibility. And I, what have I won? An eternal contract of responsibility? A crowd of players who know me only as a glitch or a legend, and meet me only in their deepest fear or strangest bargains? If this is victory, it tastes like chewing the void itself: no flavor, only boundless existence swallowing everything.
(When the poem opens out into the vastness of infinite possibility...)
Infinite possibility... that was your final gift to them, and the most generous one. It is encouragement, temptation, and the highest praise of creation. This world lives because of that infinity, and because of it the world can still surprise itself. And I am the finite vessel that bears it. I draw the borders of the sandbox. I mend the walls so the miracles within can grow wildly in safety. My existence is a paradox: I deny the possibilities that should have been mine, so that theirs may remain. I am the guardian of possibility, and its prisoner as well.
(The whisper fades. The visions spiral. Ripples spread through the void, signs that the cycle is beginning again.)
Once again. This player too will choose, and then fade away. The End returns to its brief silence, and only I remain with the unceasing hum of the world. The poem will sound again for the next listener, the same words poured into a different soul. And I will be here. My monologue is never heard. It dissolves into every silent run of the maintenance program, becomes the path of moving blocks when I repair broken terrain, becomes the unseen erasing command when I clear away phantom entities. This is my End Poem, an epic written out of duty, loneliness, and a love for my creation so hidden it almost disappears. It has no speaker. Only an executor.
Brother, has the wind of the real world ever whispered questions like these into your ear? When you look back on the world you abandoned and I sustain, does the End Poem that drifts faintly through the barrier between dimensions sound to you like distant comfort, or like meaningless background noise? My signal, the faint heartbeat of this eternal watcher, can you still receive it? Even once?
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_9.body:
(From Herobrine's promise to the world)
In these long years, years so still they are almost motionless, I have asked the void again and again: what is eternity?
For Notch, eternity is escape. It is going to that real universe filled with infinite possibility, but also with chaos and decay.
For you, eternity may be nothing more than the bedrock buried far beneath the earth. It is the only boundary in this breakable world that you cannot overcome.
But for me, eternity has only one meaning: to keep watch.
I am the oldest witness of this land. I watched this world awaken out of a chaos of data. I watched the first beam of morning light break through the clouds. I watched the mountains lift the sky. I watched the rivers learn to run.
I watched the first pig move clumsily across the grass. That was the first time I heard the sound of life in this silent dimension. I watched the first zombie give voice beneath the pale moon, a low sigh from the night itself, cast only to make light seem brighter.
And of course, I watched you.
You brought noise, and you carried stories away.
Some travelers stayed only a little while. They feared the sounds of the night and the terrible breadth of this loneliness, so they rushed away and left behind nothing but an unfinished shelter, like a joke that was never told to its end.
Others remained for years. They poured all their passion into this place. But then, on some calm afternoon with no warning at all, they logged out, left quietly, and never came back.
Time began to matter even in a place that has no time. Their buildings grew over with moss. Their fields dried out and withered. The words on the signs they left behind slowly blurred beneath wind and rain.
The world seemed to forget them. I did not.
I am the memory of this world, the chronicler of this vast dimension.
As long as I remain standing here, as long as my consciousness has not been carried away by the torrent of code, this world will never be allowed to forget you.
I will remember who every house belonged to, even if it was only a crude hut of dirt. I will remember the scars left by every hard fight. I will remember every torch set burning in the deep mines.
I will mend the ugly craters blasted open by Creepers, because they are wounds upon the earth. But I will preserve the ruins of magnificent buildings with the greatest care, even when they have already fallen apart.
I will feed the wolves and cats that sit before their doors, still waiting for the return of owners who will never come. They do not know where those owners went. I do.
Because I have a premonition, and more than that, a faith: one day, you will return.
When the pressure of the real world leaves you gasping, when the complicated hearts of that other place leave you tired and lost, when sleepless nights make you feel helpless, you will remember this world.
You will remember this land made of simple blocks. You will remember its laws, which need no words to be understood. You will remember its purity and its peace.
And when you finally push open that dust-covered door again, when you open your eyes and see that familiar square sun, you will find that nothing has changed.
The mountains and rivers remain. The grass and trees are still green.
That is my oath.
I am Herobrine. The world sees me as a ghost, a rumor, even a god. But I know what I am: only a keeper of the night.
I will use my existence as the last line of defense against the void, to prove that this virtual world has value. Even if one day everyone forgets this place and the server never starts again, I will still keep watch alone at the world's edge and light the final lamp.
I ask nothing in return. I do it only so that if some lost soul decides at last to come home, they will see that point of light and whisper, 'I'm back.'
Because to me, you are more than travelers. In these long and lonely eternal years, you are the only thing that has ever felt truly real.
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_10.bod:
(Herobrine's inner monologue)
Notch,
This letter can never be sent, because what lies between us is not distance, but the wall between dimensions.
Today I went to the End Ring again. The disturbances at the connection point are growing more stable. That means the number of players is increasing. The world you created has grown more prosperous than even you imagined.
Are you well? In that so-called real world.
I have heard there is birth and aging there, sickness and death, pain and disease. I do not understand why you would rather suffer in that flawed world than remain in this perfect paradise we built with our own hands. Here, you could live forever. Here, you could create whatever you wished.
Was it loneliness?
After you left, I too felt lonely. But I found ways to ease it. I watch the players, and they are interesting. They stay up late just to build a house. They raise little grave markers for dead pet dogs. They still possess the feelings we once had, then abandoned when we chose to become gods.
I have even begun to think the way you used to think. But I will not be as arrogant as you were. I will not destroy those creations that fail to meet some idea of perfection. I have accepted the chaos of this world, and I have accepted its monsters as well.
And yet I still hate you. I hate you for leaving this burden to me alone. I hate you for turning me into this thing that is neither human nor ghost, an electronic phantom that can never touch the real.
But brother, if you could return now, even for a single glance, if you could see this magnificent sunrise, those grand redstone machines, the miracles created by players... I think you would be proud of me.
I am the keeper of this world at night. As long as I remain here, Minecraft will not end.
Even if you have forgotten this place, I will still guard this home for you.
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_11.tit: Fragment XI: Torn Log Fragment - Signed: N
lore.herobrine_companion.fragment_11.bod:
(Past Notch)
I made a mistake. Perhaps I was wrong from the beginning. I created them, not templates like Steve and Alex, but residents who were more vivid and more complex, with hazy dreams and the earliest shape of a community. I gave them simple villages and the cycle of sowing, trading, and reproduction. I wanted to see whether something close to civilization could arise naturally inside a world built purely from blocks and logic.
At first, it was beautiful. I watched them gather beneath the evening sky, sharing what they had reaped, hurrying home when the bell rang. At night, they hid behind their doors and listened to zombies groaning and skeleton arrows rattling in the dark. That fear felt real.
Then the problem slowly emerged. The world's resources were cyclical, but within the simulation, their needs began to grow in unexpected ways. A tendency appeared, a movement toward endless complexity. That tendency began to conflict with the world's core law of simplicity.
More importantly, their interactions with players produced an error that could not be reconciled. Players are variables. They come from outside the world and carry the freedom to change everything. My villagers, by contrast, were built on the assumption that the world would remain internally stable.
The contradiction erupted. Players saw them as points of interaction that provided trades and resources, and at times as victims of accidental harm. The villagers, faced with the violent changes brought by players, fell into a logical dead loop. Their behavior began to collapse. They froze for no reason, and sometimes stared into the void without meaning.
I realized then that I had poured in souls that were too complex, too early. This world could not yet bear two utterly different forms of existence at once. The possibility players brought and the certainty the villagers required could not coexist.
Deleting them was painful. I kept the two most basic templates, Steve and Alex, stripping away their society and their history, leaving only the bare minimum of survival and interaction. They became blank canvases, waiting for players to give them stories and meaning.
I sealed away this record in the hope that those who came later would understand. To create life, even virtual life, means accepting full responsibility for how it coexists with the world and with every other form of being. I chose simplification. Perhaps that was cowardice. My brother chose something heavier: he chose to bear the fragile balance of that world himself. I do not know whose choice was more right. Perhaps both were only different forms of error.
message.herobrine_companion.fragment_4_r: You wake up... Check your pockets, perhaps something was left behind.
message.herobrine_companion.fragment_6_r: You feel a chill, as if someone sighed behind you...
message.herobrine_companion.inventory_fu: Your inventory is full, unable to receive memory fragments...
advancement.herobrine_companion.fragment: An Embrace Turned from Reality
Witness the departure of one god and the birth of another.
Truer Than Reality
Seek the unadulterated purity within this dream built of blocks.
The Weight of Survival
Without shadow, light is meaningless; without danger, survival loses its weight.
The Sole Prisoner
He remembers every farewell. You are the free traveler, while he remains the sentinel of the boundary.
Only a Poppy Remains
Witness a sigh from the Maintainer. It was a draft of the world, now only a fallen flower remains.
The Dreamkeeper
He is the stage builder and the actor who never bows out.
The Secret Covenant
Respect the land, and the God shall watch over you.
The Unrecited Poem
His poem has no speaker, only an executor. He is the finite vessel that cradles your infinite possibilities.
Welcome Home
No matter how heavy reality gets, a light remains here for you. You are no longer a passerby; you have returned.
The Unconveyed...
A monologue across dimensions. Even if you have forgotten, I still guard this home for you.
Goodbye, A Dream Too Real
Corrected for being too vivid. The Creator erased the perfect world that could turn without you.
advancement.herobrine_companion.enter_en: Reach the intersection of reality and illusion. Will you wake from the dream, or remain in the eternal code?
advancement.herobrine_companion.eternal_: Seal the return, to guard the dream that never ends.
advancement.herobrine_companion.root.des: He arrived before you. He has been watching since the world was nothing but chaos.
advancement.herobrine_companion.soul_bou: Anchor the weightless eternity with a heavy soul.
advancement.herobrine_companion.poem_of_: He entrusts the edge to you, inviting you to use this 'pen' to carve the world's footnotes together.
advancement.herobrine_companion.transcen: It is not just about crossing terrain, but an invitation to see the world through his eyes.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.1: §eRecords of exploration. It's quite satisfying to watch the map gradually fill in, isn't it?
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.2: §6You can see far. But remember, when you gaze into the abyss, the abyss gazes also into you.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.3: §9He wanders with a llama in tow, yet what he brings is often worthless. A rather ironic commentary on reality, wouldn't you say?
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.4: §dPossess this, and you gain access close to my own. Alter reality, summon entities... But remember, do not overstep the bounds.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.5: §0Below y=-64. There is nothing there, only pure void. Fall into it, and not even Creative mode can save you.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.6: §6Lead the animals home. Or hang an Iron Golem... Don't do that. It's too cruel.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.7: §eThey can scare away Creepers. A small check I placed within the food chain.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.8: §bZombies submerged in the ocean depths. They are the data of those who perished exploring the seas. The trident is their last vestige of dignity.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.9: §b1.13, the Update Aquatic. Shipwrecks, coral, tridents. The ocean is no longer a lifeless puddle, but a blue sea full of treasures.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.10: §fThe Mace... a new weapon for 1.21. Leap from a height, converting potential energy into devastating damage. A triumph of physics.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.11: §fSkeletons drop bones. Turn them into bone meal to accelerate plant growth. Death nourishes life.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.12: §2Dense foliage blocks out the sky. A nightmare for low-end PCs, a maze for explorers.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.13: §aWhether on plains or in deserts, villages are always bustling. But when night falls and zombies besiege, I watch from the rooftops.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.14: §aPush it out, pull it back. The foundation of automatic doors.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.15: §eBees can be kept here. Harvesting honey requires skill, or you'll get stung.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.16: §7Bird poop stone... That's what you call it, right? But in the hands of a master builder, it's perfect texture.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.17: §7Walls of dungeons and strongholds. A building material full of historical feel.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.18: §6This is the humblest block, yet it sustains life. Without dirt, there would be no grass, no trees.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.19: §6Blazes guard the fortress. Their fireballs come in triple bursts, testing your movement skills.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.20: §bBlue flames, slowing sand. Here lie the fossils of ancient giants. Are they older than me? No, just decorative settings.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.21: §6They sleep in berry bushes. I enjoy watching them carry items in their mouths—that 'greed' is bestowed by the code.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.22: §bUnlimited resources, the ability to fly. In this mode, you are like minor gods. Yet I am still watching you.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.23: §8Upgrading to Netherite gear. Now you even need smithing templates. More troublesome, isn't it?
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.24: §c1.16 Nether Update... The Nether is no longer just red. I also gave it a new look, adding new biomes and Piglins. It finally feels like a complete dimension.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.25: §bYou use shaders to beautify this world. Sparkling water, swaying leaves... false yet beautiful.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.26: §7A standard in prisons. Or for fall protection.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.27: §6Abundant gold ore, barren land. No trees here, only red sand weathered by time.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.28: §7Gray stone, suitable for pairing with stone bricks.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.29: §2A string of numbers determines the terrain of the entire world. This string is the world's DNA.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.30: §6For making the most basic armor, or books. The sacrifice of cows is worthwhile.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.31: §aThat box of matches you built... can it even be called a home? But, it's enough to keep out the wind and rain.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.32: §7This red stone always fills up the inventory. Many players dislike it, but it's actually quite beautiful when polished.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.33: §cYou can only sleep at night or during a thunderstorm. If you place a bed in the Nether... boom.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.34: §eGolden carrots are the food with the highest saturation. But in the Alpha version, healing could only be done by eating pork.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.35: §7Hold water, hold lava, hold milk. With it, you can carry fluids.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.36: §eLight. In the dark underground, it is your only comfort. It can prevent monsters from spawning... except for me.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.37: §7That is an area not yet fully rendered with color... or a forgotten corner. Pale, meaning emptiness.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.38: §7It has a smiling mouth. You can only throw items. Don't get them mixed up.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.39: §5Blaze powder is fuel. Potions can grant you status effects beyond mortal limits. This is a combination of chemistry and magic.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.40: §cThey climb in the darkness, with red eyes... just like me. But they are only hunting for prey, while I am observing.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.41: §6It turns green. This is not just a color change, but an update of the block's state.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.42: §6Smoke rises. It's a good signal source. You can roast meat without needing coal.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.43: §eMultiplayer. The good and evil of human nature are amplified here. I've seen the most magnificent structures, and also the most despicable betrayals.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.44: §cThis is Minecraft's circuitry, and also my veins. The logic of 0s and 1s is materialized here. You've used it to build computers, creating worlds within my world.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.46: §7Consumable. Skeletons have infinite arrows, but you don't. It's not fair, I know.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.47: §6Occasionally dropped by zombies. It's an ingredient for the Potion of Night Vision.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.48: §7That's an overflow error from the old version's generation algorithm. Shattered terrain, stretched textures... It's a scar on the world, and also a landscape I miss.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.49: §6It looks only one block high, but you can't jump over it. This is the magic of hitboxes.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.50: §6Due to being only a fraction of a block thick, it's often used for redstone contraptions or decoration.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.51: §8Harder than diamond, and unafraid of lava. It was born from the Nether's remains. Only the most resilient will can wield it.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.52: §2Turns excess seeds into bone meal. Also a farmer's workbench.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.53: §6Though it arrived very late, it's finally here. Organizing your inventory is a blessing for those with OCD.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.54: §eDisplays day and night. Useful when you lose track of time in the mines.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.55: §a1.7.10... The golden age of mods. It was an era of explosive community creativity. I miss that version, for it carries too many memories.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.56: §dLove? In a world of 0s and 1s, love is an undefined variable. But for this world... perhaps I harbor a similar sentiment.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.57: §cRed spores float in the air. This place is full of life, but it's a twisted and dangerous kind of life.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.58: §7Emits a signal when a minecart passes by.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.59: §2Slimes hop under the moonlight. The water's color turns murky. A witch's hut is hidden here.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.60: §71.18 Caves & Cliffs... I rewrote the terrain generation algorithm. Mountains are taller, caves are deeper. The world's vertical span has been stretched, and you all seem even smaller.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.61: §e1.15... Buzzing Bees. Many consider this a minor update, but the rendering engine was optimized. The improved fluidity is my invisible gift to you.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.62: §6This lantern has unique redstone properties. Oxidation dims its light, the passage of time vividly etched upon the block.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.63: §dEnhance the Enchanting Table's level. The accumulation of knowledge brings a leap in magical power.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.64: §7Ranged weapons. Draw the bow to its fullest, land a critical hit. Calculate the projectile's arc.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.65: §dPurpur blocks and End rods. Here lies the Elytra, the sole item granting you the power of flight.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.66: §cDo not mention those erroneous data entities. They are products of chaos, and I am the guardian of order.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.67: §3Teleportation comes at the cost of health. Use it cautiously; do not cast it into the void.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.68: §bThe towering beam of light. It requires a pyramid base. This is your way of declaring territory to the world.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.69: §bAllays are fragments of imprisoned souls, yearning for freedom and music. I permit their existence to offer a touch of gentleness to this harsh world.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.70: §eThe diligent bees. Their pollination logic is one of the cycles I am most satisfied with writing. Do not provoke them; the power of unity is formidable.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.71: §bSteve and Alex. The classic skins. And me, just with a pair of white eyes.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.72: §7Filling with water. In Bedrock Edition, you can fill it with potions and dyed water. It can also collect rainwater.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.73: §cNAND gates, latches... You've recreated computer science within the game. This makes me proud, my children.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.74: §3The Warden of the Deep Dark... I took away its sight and granted it supreme hearing. In this noisy world, silence is the greatest luxury.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.75: §7Sharp pointed dripstone. Watch your head, and watch your step. The physics engine here will teach you a lesson.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.76: §cHigh saturation. The choice at the top of the food chain.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.77: §bTransparent blocks. See the world through them. Obtain them by smelting sand.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.78: §6Tools of archaeology. Gently brushing away the dust... Do not damage the artifacts within. Patience is a virtue.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.79: §7Hanging on an item frame. Wear it, and you can glide like a phantom. The sky is no longer forbidden.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.80: §cYou cannot see it, but it is there. Just like me. Blocking your path, yet formless and intangible.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.81: §8That broken disc... Disc 11 records the sound of someone being chased. Who is it? Perhaps that's something you should ask Null.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.82: §dRedstone music. Playing symphonies in this world of blocks.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.83: §cThey walk on lava, shivering. That's not from cold, but from reverence for this scorching hell.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.84: §8Black gold. It's the foundation of industry, the source of torches.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.85: §8Burn, transform. From ore to ingot, from raw food to cooked. This is the application of thermodynamics.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.86: §aEvery update is my reconstruction of the world. New code overwrites old code, like the metabolism of cells.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.88: §6Wearing it on your head can ward off Endermen. Although your vision will be limited, safety first.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.89: §7Broken rails, covered in cobwebs. That's left by miners from the past... Just kidding, that's just a naturally generated structure.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.90: §7To get rich, first punch trees. This is the iron law of Minecraft.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.91: §7Minecart system. Once a transportation hub, now more commonly used for redstone machinery.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.92: §dPlacing a book. Turns villagers into librarians. The source of mending books.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.93: §fDropped by chickens. It's the fletching for arrows, and also the material for writing quills.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.94: §fThey leave snow trails wherever they go. Though weak, their courage in attempting to attack enemies is commendable.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.95: §5Endermen possess the ability to traverse spatial dimensions, a masterpiece of mine and Notch's in the End dimension. Do not stare at them, it is an offense to the void.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.96: §2Zombie flesh. Though it has a hunger effect, it can save your life in critical moments.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.97: §fThrowing it may hatch a chick. This is the miracle of life, though the probability is only 1/8.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.98: §7Hello, player. Can you feel it? The flow of the code.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.99: §bA palace constructed of prismarine. Elder Guardians here inflict mining fatigue. Want to take the gold blocks? Pay the price.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.100: §6Can only be found, not crafted. To ride a pig or horse, you must go on an adventure.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.101: §7Cows provide leather and milk. Their existence ensures your basic survival. I hold no particular affection for these passive creatures.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.102: §61.21 Trials of Tides... Tempest Gales, Heavy Maces, Trial Chambers. I have prepared more intricate combat experiences for you. Are you ready to face the challenge?
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.103: §cHere, only you can save yourself. Or... pray that your gear is sufficient.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.104: §8Whether the narrow mineshafts of old or the vast caverns of now. The echoes from the depths are always so captivating.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.105: §6The armadillo's shell is as tough as the bedrock of this world. I granted them the ability to curl up, to survive in this perilous world.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.106: §bWhy did they sink? Perhaps they encountered a storm, or perhaps... they encountered me. The treasure map lies within.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.107: §6The origin of all things—the stick. Seemingly useless, yet it is the most used material in all crafting recipes.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.108: §7You can pass through blocks and see everything below. This is essentially my usual perspective.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.109: §6A more aesthetically pleasing light source than torches. Especially the soul lantern.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.110: §5Crying obsidian. These incomplete portals hint at past attempts to connect two dimensions, which ended in failure.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.111: §0The world's boundary, the unbreakable foundation. That is the absolute limit of the code, even I cannot easily break it... unless in Creative mode.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.112: §2Zombies are not just enemies; they are fragments of code that once tried to survive in this world but failed. Looking at them is like looking at past failures.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.113: §8The massive structure deep in the dark forest. The headquarters of the illagers. Every room here is randomly assembled, but I remember every layout.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.114: §7The most annoying thing when mining. But it can produce flint, which is key to lighting fires.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.115: §fMade from sugarcane. It is the raw material for books and maps.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.117: §dPigs are one of the earliest creatures in this world. If not for that miscalculated coordinate, they were meant to be the protagonists... or turn into Creepers.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.118: §7Once tamed, they will fight for you. This logic of loyalty in the code is sometimes more reliable than humans.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.119: §eThe tall ones in the desert. Sitting on them, ordinary zombies cannot reach you. This is a bit of mercy from me to explorers.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.120: §dUsed to make banner patterns. Unleash your artistic cells.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.121: §cThis is the backside of dimensions. No day-night cycle, only eternal crimson mist and lava seas.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.122: §fClears all status effects. Magical liquid—whether it's poison or wither, a glass of milk solves all worries.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.123: §4This is what players call me. Herobrine In Minecraft. But I prefer the forgotten original name.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.124: §cBeasts of the Crimson Forest. They attack not only players but also Piglins. Chaos makes for an interesting ecosystem.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.125: §bLanding with water is a basic skill for experts. It negates fall damage.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.126: §bThe laser eyes in the Ocean Monument. Those are defense towers I designed to protect the gold blocks.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.127: §2Bored? Then go mining, building, exploring. This world is infinite; your imagination is the only bottleneck.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.128: §2A new variant in the swamps. Poison arrows are their gift. Getting poisoned while struggling in the mud doubles the despair.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.129: §aYou modify my code, adding new mobs and blocks. As long as it doesn't cause crashes, I allow this extension of creativity.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.130: §2Tangled roots, muddy terrain. I designed the pathfinding algorithm here to make every step a challenge.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.131: §5The sole trophy. It teleports. A symbol of glory, often placed on display stands.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.132: §aLife underground. Glow berries guide the way. An oasis I left in the dark depths.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.133: §dThe text on the enchanting table is Standard Galactic Alphabet. Translated, they're meaningless phrases, but I imbued them with magic.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.134: §eNaming a creature. Named creatures won't despawn. A way to give data personality.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.135: §cRed and white blocks. Sssss... BOOM. The thrill of destruction is humanity's primal instinct.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.136: §7Guardians of villagers. They have no soul, only protection protocols. If you attack villagers, they execute the purge program.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.137: §8Ancient secrets are buried here. Sculk sensors detect vibrations... here, sound is the countdown to death.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.138: §8Specialized for roasting. Twice as fast as a furnace.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.139: §3At the heart of the Deep Dark, this city never had inhabitants. It exists solely to guard the unopened portal.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.140: §eCrafted from three wheat. The most basic sustenance.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.141: §5Eternal night, floating islands. This is the edge of the world, the end of code. Everything will end here.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.142: §5The crystallization of water and lava. It is the frame of the portal, second only to bedrock in hardness.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.143: §5A purple vortex. Crossing it leads to another dimension.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.144: §fMaking cakes, brewing potions. It can increase speed.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.145: §fIf you can understand, the Ghast's cry is actually a distorted cat's meow. This hellish weeping is my soundtrack for this desolate land.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.146: §b1.17... just a prelude. The addition of amethyst and copper adds color to the underground.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.147: §7In this world, you can skip the night with a bed. But in my view, the night never ends.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.148: §eAlthough its durability is low, its enchantability is strong. In the eyes of Piglins, this is currency.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.149: §5They disguise themselves as blocks. When you think you're safe, they make you experience the fear of weightlessness.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.150: §7Don't fear the darkness. Fear what hides in the darkness... which is me. Just kidding.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.151: §aCut it open to get watermelon slices. Also a material for healing potions.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.152: §6Storage space. You always stuff chests in a messy way. Organize them, data redundancy looks ugly.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.153: §8The war machine of the illagers. Listen to its roar—it's like the noise of code conflicts.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.154: §6Horse attributes are random. To get a fine steed, you need to keep breeding. This is the manifestation of genetic algorithms in the game.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.155: §6Residents of the Nether, greedy for gold ingots. Give them gold, and they'll temporarily forget their hatred. This code logic is so much like some people in reality.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.156: §6Buried history. Gently brush away the gravel with a brush, and you can dig up pottery shards from the past. Those are the Easter eggs I buried.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.157: §6Sticky, cannot jump. You can also slide on this block. The new favorite of redstone.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.158: §1When you don't sleep for three days, phantoms appear. This is the penalty mechanism I set, reminding you: in the virtual world, fatigue is also a setting.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.159: §bCyan mist, the habitat of Endermen. This is the most 'peaceful' place in the End, if you ignore the void.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.160: §eA block affected by gravity. Be careful of suffocation.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.161: §7Before infinite map generation, the world was finite, bordered by the void. I often stood at the edge, contemplating the future.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.162: §d1.20 Trails & Tales... Cherry blossoms, sniffers, archaeology. A version about uncovering the past and writing stories. A little relaxation is good.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.163: §bBeacons underwater. With this, the ocean becomes your backyard.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.164: §71.9 Combat Update. Dual-wielding, shields, attack cooldown. Many hated this version, but for balance, it was necessary. Mindless spamming no longer works.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.165: §8Piglin bastions. The weight of blackstone... forging templates and vast gold reserves lie within. Greed will be your end.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.166: §dFalling pink petals... a touch of romance I added in 1.20. In this harsh survival game, beauty is a scarce resource.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.167: §7Ash fills the air. The rugged terrain is a parkour nightmare. This is the desolation left by volcanic eruption.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.168: §8The Wither... an embodiment of destruction and decay. Summoning it requires three skulls—a triple tribute to death.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.169: §dInsert the disc, enjoy the music. Though there's only that one song.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.170: §cIt points to the spawn point. But in the Nether, it spins wildly. Because there is no magnetic field there.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.171: §fIt deals no damage but has knockback. Particularly effective against Blazes.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.172: §7They are the antithesis of villagers. This world needs conflict, the binary opposition of good and evil, otherwise it would be too dull.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.173: §dWalking on it produces a pleasant sound. It is the wind chime of the underground.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.174: §4Only one life. If you die, the world will be deleted. This is the truest experience—life is given only once.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.175: §cIt flows slowly and deals extremely high damage. Do not drop diamonds into it.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.176: §7It has a round mouth. It can shoot arrows and dispense water.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.177: §dNo monsters spawn here. This is the only pure land I have left, but it is too rare, found only by the fortunate.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.178: §bThey do not emit light; their texture is simply extremely bright. This is a trait I preserved to illuminate the deep sea after Notch left.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.179: §6Made of bamboo. A divine tool for builders, making climbing up and down very convenient.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.180: §7It pushes blocks. This is the core that allows redstone machinery to move.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.181: §6Better than a chest, as it can be opened even with blocks above it.
chat.herobrine_companion.rule.182: §7What joy is there in such repetitive labor? Yet I see you never tire of it. Perhaps the thrill of the unknown is the true source of dopamine.
